headline: Lula wins a fourth term as Brazil's president

sources.title: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil's president, beating Flávio Bolsonaro in runoff (CBS News)
Lula holds off far right with victory in Brazil presidential election (Al Jazeera)
Lula re-elected in Brazil as Bolsonaro rejects results (CBC News)

chunks.text: President Lula has {{pulled off}} a [[comeback]]. On October 25, 2026, Brazil held a presidential runoff, a second vote between the top two candidates. Lula {{held off}} a [[strong challenge]] from Senator Bolsonaro, the son of a former president. Brazil's [[electoral court]], which runs elections, said Lula won 51.8 percent, about 4.4 million votes more than Bolsonaro. Lula {{fell behind}} in the first round on October 4. Since [[military rule]] ended in 1985, no candidate had won the [[presidency]] after coming second in the first round.

verbs.wrong: To ask for a vote recount
verbs.why: Small teams sometimes pull off big wins. She often pulls off hard tasks at work. President Lula has pulled off a comeback.

verbs.correct: To stop a rival from winning
verbs.wrong: To share power with a rival
verbs.why: The home team holds off a late attack in most games. A good runner holds off the others near the finish line. Lula held off a strong challenge from Senator Bolsonaro, the son of a former president.

verbs.correct: To be losing to a rival
verbs.wrong: To refuse to join a debate
verbs.why: Some candidates fall behind after a bad debate. A team falls behind when the other side scores first. Lula fell behind in the first round on October 4.

chunks.text: Election day ended in [[confusion]] at [[polling stations]]. Just before closing time, a Supreme Court [[justice]], a judge on Brazil's top court, ordered a two-hour [[extension]] of voting. Both campaigns had asked for more time. Lula's [[allies]] said bus service had been {{scaled back}} in some [[working-class]] areas. Bolsonaro's team said heavy rain slowed voting in the south. Voting {{wrapped up}} two hours late, which {{held up}} the count. At one station, [[voting machines]] had already been {{turned off}} and could not be restarted.

verbs.correct: To offer less of a service
verbs.wrong: To make a service cost more
verbs.why: Many cities scale back train service at night. Some stores scale back their hours in winter. Lula's allies said bus service had been scaled back in some working-class areas.

verbs.wrong: To move to a new building
verbs.why: Our meetings usually wrap up before noon. The school year wraps up in early June. Voting wrapped up two hours late, which held up the count.

verbs.wrong: To check something a second time
verbs.why: Bad weather often holds up flights. A long line holds up everyone behind it. Voting wrapped up two hours late, which held up the count.

verbs.correct: To make a machine stop running
verbs.wrong: To fix a machine that is broken
verbs.why: I turn off my computer every night. She turns off the lights when she leaves a room. At one station, voting machines had already been turned off and could not be restarted.

chunks.text: Bolsonaro has not [[conceded defeat]]. He said he would ask the courts to {{throw out}} the election. He {{pushed back}} hard and called the extension [[unacceptable]]. He said the justice changed the rules while people were still voting. He {{pointed out}} that the justice once worked as Lula's lawyer. The head of the electoral court also criticized the extension, but said it did not change the result.

verbs.correct: To say a result does not count
verbs.why: Judges sometimes throw out a case with weak evidence. The league throws out a game result when a team breaks the rules. He said he would ask the courts to throw out the election.
Parents often push back when a school changes the rules. Workers push back against longer hours. He pushed back hard and called the extension unacceptable.

verbs.correct: To mention a fact to others
verbs.why: My teacher points out my spelling mistakes. A good guide points out the oldest buildings in town. He pointed out that the justice once worked as Lula's lawyer.

chunks.text: [[Celebrations]] {{broke out}} in Brazil's two biggest cities. Lula was president for two [[terms]], from 2003 to 2010, and again from 2023. His fourth term is due to {{kick off}} on January 5, 2027, when he will be 81. Right-wing parties, Lula's main opponents, are strong in the new Congress, which makes Brazil's laws. He said he would work with [[lawmakers]] to pass his plans.

verbs.why: Applause breaks out when the home team scores. Laughter often breaks out at family dinners. Celebrations broke out in Brazil's two biggest cities.

verbs.wrong: To be moved to a new date
verbs.why: The summer festival kicks off every July. Our workday kicks off with a short meeting. His fourth term is due to kick off on January 5, 2027, when he will be 81.

mainIdea.s: Brazil's president won the runoff and a fourth term after coming second in the first round. His rival has not accepted the result and wants a court to cancel it over the late voting hours.
mainIdea.why: Lula pulled off a comeback after he fell behind in the first round. Bolsonaro pushed back hard and said he would ask the courts to throw out the election.

mainIdea.s: Brazil's leader kept the lead he took in the first round and won again by a wide margin. The losing senator now asks judges to cancel the vote because voting stayed open two extra hours.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Lula fell behind in the first round. He won the runoff by about 4.4 million votes, with 51.8 percent.

mainIdea.s: Brazil's electoral court has delayed the presidential runoff by one week because of heavy rain. Officials say voters in the south need more time to reach their polling places safely.
mainIdea.why: The runoff was held on October 25. Voting wrapped up two hours late, and Lula held off a strong challenge to win.

tf.s: Lula pulled off a comeback to win Brazil's presidential runoff.
tf.why: He came second in the first round, then beat Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of a former president, by about 4.4 million votes.

tf.s: Lula came first in the first round of the election.
tf.why: Lula fell behind Bolsonaro in the first round on October 4, then won the runoff.

tf.s: A Supreme Court justice kept voting open for extra time.
tf.why: Both campaigns asked for more time, and voting wrapped up two hours late.

tf.s: Bolsonaro accepted the result and congratulated Lula.
tf.why: Bolsonaro has not conceded defeat. He pushed back hard and called the extension unacceptable.

tf.s: Bolsonaro said he would ask the courts to throw out the election.
tf.why: He has not conceded defeat and says the justice changed the rules while people were still voting.

tf.s: Lula said he would ignore Congress and govern alone.
tf.why: Right-wing parties are strong in Congress, but Lula said he would work with lawmakers. His fourth term is due to kick off on January 5, 2027.

lines.text: Did you see the news from Brazil? Lula {{pulled off}} a comeback.
I did. He {{fell behind}} in the first round, right?
Yes. Bolsonaro was ahead by more than two million votes on October 4.
In a way. He got 51.8 percent in the runoff.
It was. Voting {{wrapped up}} two hours late, so the count was {{held up}}.
A Supreme Court justice kept voting open for two more hours. Both campaigns asked for more time.
I'd be [[on the edge of my seat]] all evening.
Same here. And some voting machines had already been {{turned off}}.
He {{pushed back}} hard. He says he will ask the courts to {{throw out}} the result.
Losing like that must be [[a tough pill to swallow]] for his supporters.
For sure. Meanwhile, celebrations {{broke out}} in the big cities.
When does the new term {{kick off}}?
On January 5. Either way, it was [[a long night]] for a lot of Brazilians.

expressions.def: A contest so close that people feel nervous until the end

expressions.def: Something bad that is hard to accept

expressions.def: A night that feels long because you stay awake, busy or worried
